new_statements.rule_in_words: In Sumambuq (Tagal) Murut, as in Timugon, word stress is non-contrastive and falls on the penultimate syllable: /kadui/ is stressed [kadúi] (penult /du/) while /kanuy/ with a final glide is [kánuy] (penult /ka/); Prentice's Sumambuq phonology section lists no stress difference from the Timugon pattern (penultimate strong stress, weak stress on the initial syllable of long words).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing stated for Sumambuq; the presupposed Timugon pattern (p. 14) has weak stress on the first syllable when it is separated from the strong stress by two or more syllables, and weak stress replacing strong stress on a word subordinate to another within a phrase.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Sumambuq. (Timugon p. 14 notes 'very few exceptions', cross-referring to 2.3.3.3, e.g. some particles stressed on the last syllable.)
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress in citation forms; the Tagal evidence is an in-passing remark with two stress-marked words plus the chapter's stated method of describing only departures from Timugon, not an explicit Tagal stress rule. Data from the Tumaniq (Tomani), Mauligan and Tagol (Salarom) subdialects, fieldwork 1960s.
new_statements.identity_note: Prentice 1971 describes the 'Sumambuq dialect of Highland Murut' (his preferred name for Tagal/Tagol/'Pensiangan Murut'), from the Tumaniq (Tomani river), Mauligan (Meligan) and Tagol (Salarom village) subdialects -- all within Glottolog taga1273 / ISO mvv. His 'Highland Murut language' also includes Paluan (Glottolog palu1253? = ISO plz, a separate language) and Alumbis (an mvv dialect in Ethnologue); the quoted remark is specific to Sumambuq. The explicit penultimate-stress rule he relies on is stated for Timugon Murut (timu1262), so the Tagal reading is partly by the author's stated 'differences-only' method.

sources.locator: sec. 10.3.2 'The Sumambuq dialect', p. 292 (PDF p. 304); with sec. 10.0 p. 274 and sec. 2.2.1.1 p. 14 (Timugon rule that the outline studies presuppose)
sources.note: For Sumambuq (= Tagal) the only stress remark is on p. 292: Lees's analysis of final /w y/ as /u i/ 'fails to account for the stress differences in such pairs as /kadúi/ porcupine and /kánuy/ eagle' (accents in the scan) -- i.e. stress is penultimate (ka.DÚ.i vs KÁ.nuy). Sec. 10.3.2.1 Phonology gives inventory and /b d g/ allophony only; sec. 10.0 says outlines describe only features differing from Timugon, whose rule (p. 14) is non-phonemic strong stress on the penultimate syllable, weak stress on the first syllable when two or more syllables precede the strong stress.
